title.rendered: Thanks Be to God, Who Gives Us the Victory: The Win Already Won | The Thankful Heart, Day 11

excerpt.rendered: 1 Corinthians 15:57 thanks God for the victory given through Jesus Christ. Day 11 of The Thankful Heart gives thanks from a battle already won.

content.rendered:
Paul does not say God will give us the victory if we fight hard enough. He says God gives it, present tense, through Jesus. We do not give thanks hoping to win. We give thanks because the win has already been handed to us.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, November 25, 2026 | The Thankful Heart, Day 11

Today’s Scripture

“But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ. Therefore, my beloved brethren, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, knowing that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.”
1 Corinthians 15:57-58 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

1 Corinthians 15 is the great resurrection chapter. Paul has spent more than fifty verses explaining that Christ has truly risen from the dead, that He is the firstfruits of all who will rise, and that death itself has been defeated. Then he lifts his eyes and taunts the last enemy: “O Death, where is your sting? O Hades, where is your victory?” And straight after the taunt comes the thanksgiving: “But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory.”

Notice who wins the victory. Not us. God gives it. The word translated “victory” is the Greek nikos (νῖκος), the same word Paul has just used to say death is swallowed up in victory. In English, victory can sound like a contest still in play, but nikos speaks of the results of a conquest, a triumph already won, and here God places it in our hands as a gift. And notice how: “through our Lord Jesus Christ.” Jesus fought the battle we could never fight. He took the sting of death, which is sin, into His own body on the cross. He met the strength of sin, which is the law, and fulfilled it completely. Then He walked out of the grave. The victory is His, and He hands it to everyone who belongs to Him.

This changes how we face every battle. We do not fight for victory; we fight from victory. When temptation comes, when fear rises, when the news is bad, we are not hoping that somehow we might come out on top. We are standing on ground Jesus has already taken. Romans 8:37 says that in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us. Our thanksgiving is the sound of soldiers who already know the outcome.

Then Paul draws the practical conclusion in verse 58: “Therefore”, because the victory is secure, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord. The nurse on a long shift in Manila, the teacher in Nairobi, the pastor in a small church in Sao Paulo: “your labor is not in vain in the Lord.” Nothing done for Him is wasted, because the resurrection guarantees that what is sown in Him will rise.

So wherever you are fighting today, start with thanks. “Thanks be to God, who gives me the victory through Jesus.” Say it before you see the outcome. Say it in the middle of the struggle. It is not wishful thinking. It is the most realistic thing a believer can say, because it rests on an empty tomb.

How the Thankful Heart Stands

It fights from victory, not for victory. Jesus has already won, and God gives the victory to us through Him.

It mocks the last enemy. Death has lost its sting because Christ is risen.

It labours with confidence. Nothing done in the Lord is ever in vain.

Declaration

Thanks be to God, who gives me the victory through my Lord Jesus Christ (1 Corinthians 15:57). Lord, I thank You that Jesus has defeated sin and death, and that in all things I am more than a conqueror through Him who loved me (Romans 8:37). I stand steadfast and immovable, abounding in Your work, because I know my labour is not in vain in You. I do not fight for victory; I give thanks from it. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
